title: Stand-up, planning and retrospective: the meetings, and what they are for

videos.script: Every team has meetings, and every team complains about them. Most of the complaining is about meetings that have forgotten what they are for. {{complain}} This lesson takes the three you will meet in almost any team, the daily stand-up, sprint planning and the retrospective, together with the review that sits between the last two, and asks one question of each. What would go wrong if we did not have it? {{question}} The stand-up exists because a blocked card nobody mentions stays blocked. Fifteen minutes, every day, and it is not a report to a manager. {{standup}} Planning exists because a team that takes on more than it can finish finishes less. It turns a backlog into a promise the team can actually keep. {{planning}} The review exists so the people who asked for something see it working, while there is still time to change it. {{review}} And the retrospective exists because the way a team works is also something that can be improved, but only if somebody stops once in a while to look at it. {{retro}} You will learn what each one needs, what it produces, and the signs that it has turned into the kind of meeting people complain about. {{title}}
